correctness.rationale: Definitions and all quantifiers specify odd dimensions at least five and every s in [0,1]. The cut region is exactly the determinant-two inverse image of an n-simplex; Euclidean base and removed-edge facet areas are derived from perpendicular heights, and the untouched coordinate faces are justified. Ambient area is determined using path alternating permutations and the origin-based pyramid identity. The derivative log quotient factorizes as (n-1)s^(n-2)(bs-a)/((1-a s^(n-1))(1-b s^n)), with positive denominators. This proves the unique interior pentagonal optimum and all higher odd-dimensional endpoint optima; exact rational Gram and independent Qhull diagnostics tested n=3,5,7,9 without being used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The odd-hole inequality is a canonical, motivated integrality cut. The theorem determines its entire Euclidean metric cost rather than a selected coordinate or arbitrary slice; it identifies a genuine five-versus-seven dimensional reversal and an intermediate pentagon cut more isoperimetrically efficient than either full fractional or integral endpoint. This sharp optimization is meaningful for geometric evaluation of valid inequalities, even though the simplex cap and volume prerequisites are known.
